concepts.concept_description: Adding and using the Video Sensing extension to incorporate a live camera feed and motion detection into a Scratch project.
Using the 'turn video on' block to activate the user's camera when the program starts.
Using the 'set video transparency to' block to control the visibility of the live video feed on the stage. A value of 0 makes the video fully visible.
Using the 'video motion on sprite' reporter block to get a numerical value that represents the amount of motion detected by the camera.
Using the 'when green flag clicked' event block to trigger a script that initializes the project, such as turning on the video.
Using a 'forever' loop to make a script run continuously, allowing the program to constantly check for a condition like user motion.
Using the 'next costume' block to cycle through a sprite's different appearances, which in this project, function as different face filters.
Using the 'wait until' control block to pause a script's execution until a specific condition, like video motion exceeding a certain threshold, becomes true.
Creating a condition by comparing a sensor value (video motion) with a number using a comparison operator (e.g., 'video motion > 50').
Using the '>' operator to check if the motion detected by the video sensor is greater than a specific value (e.g., 50) to trigger an action.
Using the 'wait' block to pause the script for a specified number of seconds, which keeps a filter on the screen for a set duration before the loop repeats.
Using the 'when this sprite clicked' event to provide an alternative way for the user to interact with the program, such as manually changing to the next filter.
The technique of creating multiple costumes for a single sprite to represent different states or effects, such as the various face filters (hat, glasses, mustache).
Utilizing the built-in Scratch Paint Editor to draw and customize new costumes for a sprite, such as drawing the hat, glasses, and mustache filters.
Understanding that program actions are triggered by events, such as the green flag click, a sprite click, or a sensor value crossing a threshold.
